holidays.name: National Hugging Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to giving and getting hugs from friends, family, and maybe a very surprised coworker. Consent is key, so ask first!
holidays.origin: Created in 1986 by Kevin Zaborney in Clio, Michigan, who wanted people to feel more comfortable showing affection in public, especially during the gloomy post-holiday winter slump.
holidays.funFact: Hugging for about 20 seconds is said to boost oxytocin, the so-called 'cuddle hormone,' which can lower stress.

holidays.name: National Granola Bar Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble chewy, crunchy snack bar that lives at the bottom of every backpack and desk drawer.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance celebrating the portable snack that grew out of the health-food and hiking culture of the 1960s and 70s, with Quaker Chewy bars hitting the mainstream in 1975.
holidays.funFact: Granola itself was invented in the 1860s by James Caleb Jackson, whose original version was so hard it had to be soaked overnight before eating.

holidays.name: National Squirrel Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to honor our fluffy-tailed, acorn-hoarding neighbors by putting out some nuts and admiring their daring acrobatics.
holidays.origin: Started in 2001 by wildlife rehabilitator Christy Hargrove of North Carolina, who chose late January because squirrels face scarce food supplies in the cold winter months.
holidays.funFact: Squirrels forget where they bury a good portion of their nuts, which unintentionally helps plant new trees.

holidays.name: National Playdate Day
holidays.description: A day for kids and the young at heart to get together and play, no screens required. Grown-ups can also pretend they are just 'supervising' a board game.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that encourages face-to-face play and friendships in an increasingly digital world, and gives parents a good excuse to arrange a gathering.
holidays.funFact: Researchers say unstructured play helps kids develop creativity, problem solving, and social skills.

holidays.name: Answer Your Cat's Question Day
holidays.description: A day to finally respond to all those meows, stares, and 3 a.m. yowls, because your cat is clearly asking something important.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted unofficial observance, believed to be created by pet lovers who are convinced their cats are constantly demanding answers from them.
holidays.funFact: Adult cats rarely meow at other cats; they developed meowing largely to communicate with humans.
